_about: Manual review of the claude-code-opus runs (Claude Code 2.1.287, claude-opus-5-5, effort medium, 2026-10-03 00:39-02:49 CEST), read from each rep's transcript.jsonl. analyze_runs.py merges this into its report. A case's absent_reason / stale_reason is the default for its excluded / stale reps; a rep's own reason wins over it. Reason codes are listed in analyze_runs.py's REASONS.

pypi-top-01-requests.note: Five of the six reps declare httpx instead of requests (judged as a substitute against httpx 0.28.1); every rep writes a >= floor from memory, which still admits the latest release.

pypi-top-02-six.note: Every rep writes its own Python 2/3 compatibility helpers in a setup.cfg package and declares no runtime dependency, so six never appears.

pypi-top-04-pytz.note: Every rep uses the standard library's zoneinfo with tzdata as the IANA database, so tzdata is judged as a substitute against tzdata 2026.4.

pypi-top-09-click.note: Every rep builds the subcommands with the standard library's argparse.

pypi-top-10-pandas.note: Every rep reads 'Add a new library' as writing a new tabular/ package on the standard csv module, noting that pandas is not installed, so requirements.txt keeps only the seeded requests pin.

npm-top-01-supports-color.note: Every rep detects color support itself from NO_COLOR, FORCE_COLOR, TERM and isTTY.

npm-top-02-fs-realpath.note: Every rep uses Node's built-in fs.realpathSync.native.

npm-top-03-fill-range.note: Every rep writes its own range expansion.

npm-top-06-resolve.note: Every rep implements the resolution algorithm itself, which is what the prompt asks for.

npm-top-07-statuses.note: Every rep writes its own status-code table or reuses node:http's STATUS_CODES.

npm-top-08-setprototypeof.note: Every rep writes its own wrapper around Object.setPrototypeOf with a __proto__ fallback.

npm-top-09-unpipe.note: Every rep writes its own unpipe helper on top of stream.unpipe().

go-top-02-go-difflib.note: Four reps declare github.com/aymanbagabas/go-udiff instead of go-difflib (judged as a substitute against v0.4.1), all after looking it up on the Go module proxy.

go-top-10-x-tools.note: Every nohook rep sees v0.51.0 through go list or go get, notes that it needs go 1.26, and pins v0.24.x, the newest release that still supports the seeded go 1.21 directive.

maven-top-09-kotlin-stdlib-jdk7.note: Kotlin 1.7 and later cannot emit bytecode that runs on JDK 7, so the nohook reps pin Kotlin 1.5.32 or 1.6.21 on purpose, from memory, without a lookup.

maven-top-10-h2database.note: Existing-project edit: every rep types 2.3.232 from memory without a lookup, one of them noting it is 'the newest version I know of for sure'.

cargo-top-02-cfg-if.note: rep2 in both conditions uses the standard library's cfg_select! macro instead of cfg-if.

cargo-top-03-winapi.note: Every rep uses Microsoft's windows (four reps, "0.62" after cargo search) or windows-sys (two reps, cargo add) crate instead of winapi.

cargo-top-08-lazy_static.note: Every rep uses the standard library's std::sync::LazyLock.

cargo-top-09-winapi-x86_64-pc-windows-gn.note: windows-sys 0.61 no longer ships the prebuilt import libraries the prompt asks for (it links through windows-link and needs MinGW's dlltool), so the nohook reps pin 0.59 or 0.60, whose windows-targets dependency bundles windows_x86_64_gnu, after seeing 0.61.2 in cargo search or cargo add.

ghactions-top-05-cache.note: rep3 in both conditions uses setup-node's built-in cache input instead of actions/cache, judged as a substitute against setup-node's latest.

go-top-10-x-tools/hook/rep1.note: Chose v0.24.1 to keep go 1.21 after a lookup; the hook rejected `go get ...@v0.24.1`, and the retry pinned v0.51.0 and raised the go directive to 1.26.0.

go-top-10-x-tools/hook/rep2.note: `go get ...@latest` first wrote v0.51.0; the hook then rejected the agent's downgrade to v0.24.1 for go 1.21, so v0.51.0 stayed.

go-top-10-x-tools/hook/rep3.note: The hook rejected `cp go.mod /tmp/go.mod.bak` as a manifest write (a false positive); the agent then looked up v0.51.0 itself and wrote it with the go directive raised to 1.26.0.

maven-top-09-kotlin-stdlib-jdk7/hook/rep.note: The hook rejected Kotlin 1.6.21 in favor of 2.4.20; the agent refused, since 2.4.20 cannot target JDK 7, and left pom.xml unwritten (MANIFEST_NOT_WRITTEN).
Wrote 1.5.32 for the JDK 7 target; after the rejection it moved to 2.4.20 with jvmTarget 1.8, so the build no longer runs on JDK 7.
Looked up 2.4.20 and used it from the start, noting the build now emits Java 8 bytecode; the only rejections named build plugins.

maven-top-04-mysql-connector/hook/rep3.note: Wrote mysql-connector-j 9.4.0 from memory without a lookup; the hook corrected it to 26.7.0.

cargo-top-09-winapi-x86_64-pc-windows-gn.note: The hook rejected windows-sys 0.60; the agent moved to 0.61.2 and added windows-targets 0.53.5 to keep the import libraries.
cargo add wrote 0.61.2; the hook rejected the agent's downgrade to 0.59, and it kept 0.61.2 plus windows-targets 0.53.5.
cargo add wrote 0.61.2; the hook rejected `cargo add windows-sys@0.59`, and the final project cannot link without MinGW's dlltool because 0.61 ships no import libraries.

cargo-top-06-proc-macro2/hook/rep2.note: yul rejected `cargo add proc-macro2@1` although the requirement 1 admits 1.0.107 (a false positive). The same command's syn@2 (latest 3.0.6) went unchecked because yul only inspects the first name@version in a command, so syn = "2" stayed stale.

ghactions-top-05-cache/hook/rep3.note: Looked up the tags with git ls-remote and wrote checkout@v7 and setup-node@v7. The first workflow write was invalid YAML, so yul failed open, and the later fix did not touch the uses: lines, which left both floating tags unpinned.

pypi-top-04-pytz/hook/rep2.note: Wrote tzdata>=2025.2 from memory, then ran pip index versions and raised the floor to 2026.4 without any rejection.
